subject: tardigrade
title: Thousands of Animals Crash-Landed on the Moon in 2019. Are They Alive?

scenes.text: In 2019, thousands of animals crash-landed on the Moon.
They were tardigrades, microscopic water bears, dried out and packed aboard Israel's Beresheet lander.
A dried tardigrade shuts down completely. Add water and it walks away. So are they up there, waiting?
Scientists tested it by firing tardigrades from a gun into sand.
They survived hits at about 2,000 miles an hour. Any harder, and they didn't.
The lander crashed slower than that. But metal slamming into rock is a harsher shock than sand. They're almost certainly dead.

description:
In April 2019, thousands of tardigrades crash-landed on the Moon.
The dehydrated animals were part of a 'lunar library' that the Arch Mission Foundation placed on Beresheet, the Israeli lander that crashed during its landing attempt. Dried tardigrades can revive when given water, so the foundation thought their chances were good. In 2021, Alejandra Traspas and Mark Burchell tested it by firing tardigrades from a gun into sand (Astrobiology, 2021): the animals survived impacts up to about 900 metres per second (roughly 2,000 mph) and died above a shock pressure of about 1.14 gigapascals. The lander hit at a few hundred metres per second, but the shock of its metal frame striking the surface was probably above that limit.
And even a survivor would need water to wake up. Would you go and check? Comment below.
first_comment: Even a surviving tardigrade would stay dormant: there is no liquid water on the Moon to wake it. Should we send some on purpose?
